questions.solution:
Solution:

Statement I: Heavy rains → water logging in city

Statement II: Prices of vegetables increased sharply

Both could be effects of a common cause : heavy rains can cause water logging and affect vegetable supply → price rise.

Answer: Both Statements I and II are effects of a common cause ✅

Additional Information:

Heavy rains is the underlying common factor.

Water logging and vegetable price rise are two separate outcomes of the same cause.

Read both the statements and select the most appropriate answer. Seven boxes A, B, P, T, V, X, and Z are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. How many boxes are kept between P and B? (I) Exactly three boxes are kept above T. Z is kept third from the bottom. (II) Only X is kept below B. Only V is kept above P.

questions.solution:
Solution:

Statement I: Gives positions of T and Z only → cannot determine boxes between P and B .

Statement II:

Only X is below B → B must be 2nd from bottom .

Only V is above P → P must be 2nd from top .

Total boxes = 7 → 3 boxes between P and B ✅

(Data in Statement II alone is sufficient while Statement I is not)

questions.solution:
Statement I

Only four people sit between Z and V → With 6 people, Z and V must occupy positions 1 & 6 (order unknown).

R sits immediately left of Z → Relative position of R to Z known.

Analysis:

Z = 1 or 6, V = other end → multiple possibilities

T’s position is not fixed → cannot determine who is immediately left of T

✅ Statement I alone not sufficient

Statement II

Only two people sit to the left of F → F = position 3

Only two people sit to the right of T → T = position 4

Analysis:

Positions fixed: T = 4 → immediate left of T = position 3 → F sits there

✅ Statement II alone sufficient

questions.solution:
Answer: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient while Statement I is not.

Why:

Statement I:
“Only P is older than K” ⇒ K is 2nd oldest; “E older than R” ⇒ E > R.
No info about V’s position ⇒ not sufficient .

Statement II:
“Exactly two people are younger than E” ⇒ E is 3rd (two above, two below).
“V is older than R, but younger than E” ⇒ Order fixes as: (K, P) > E > V > R .
Thus, people older than V are K, P, E ⇒ 3 .
This is uniquely determined ⇒ sufficient .

Six people, G, I, J, K, R, and W are sitting in a row, facing the north. How many people sit to the left of I?
(I) Only four people sit between K and I. J sits to the immediate left of W.

questions.solution:
Answer: Both statements I and II together (and not I alone or II alone) are sufficient.

Why:

I alone: “Only four between K and I” ⇒ K & I are at the two ends (1 and 6). “J immediately left of W.”
I could be at 1 (0 left) or 6 (5 left) → not unique ⇒ insufficient .

II alone: “One between G & K” and “one between G & J” ⇒ G must be 3 or 4 with {K, J} = {1,5} or {2,6}.
I’s position is unconstrained ⇒ insufficient .

I + II together:
From II: either

G=3 with { K,J } ={ 1,5} (fails with I’s “J left of W” once you place I at the other end), or

G=4 with { K,J } ={ 2,6} .
From I: K and I at ends ⇒ with K=6 ⇒ I=1 ; also J=2, W=3 (since J is immediately left of W). Arrangement becomes:
1 I, 2 J, 3 W, 4 G, 5 R, 6 K (unique).

Thus the number of people to the left of I is 0 , and this is determined only when combining I & II.

questions.solution:
Solution:

Given logic: Take the number, multiply by 2, subtract 1, then square

Example check:

5 → (5 × 2 − 1)² = (10 − 1)² = 9² = 81 ✅

2 → (2 × 2 − 1)² = (4 − 1)² = 3² = 9 ✅

Apply for 6:

(6 × 2 − 1)² = (12 − 1)² = 11² = 121

Answer: Data in Statement I alone is sufficient while Statement II is not.

Why:

I: “J is third from the bottom” ⇒ J at position 3 (from bottom). “Exactly three boxes between A and J” ⇒ A must be at position 7 (top). So topmost = A . Sufficient.

II: “C immediately above J” and “No box below V” ⇒ V is at the bottom, but topmost could be several boxes depending on J and C’s positions. Not sufficient.

questions.solution:
Answer: I weakens while II strengthens the statement

Why:

Argument I cites strong demand from seniors for accessible ground-floor apartments → this goes against a blanket prohibition ⇒ weakens.

Argument II highlights a safety risk (flooding of basements/ground floors in monsoon) → supports the safety-based prohibition ⇒ strengthens.
